subject: Chevalier Theater Restoration Funding
overview: The committee held its annual public hearing to collect community input on Community Preservation Act priorities and approved a $100,000 emergency grant for the Chevalier Theater. Representatives from city departments presented long-term needs for affordable housing redevelopments, park improvements, and school facility restorations.

items.title: Annual Public Hearing Presentation
items.summary: The chair provided an overview of the Community Preservation Act (CPA), past projects, and the projected $2 million available for the upcoming fiscal year across housing, open space, and historic preservation.

items.title: Survey and Outreach Review
items.summary: Staff reviewed preliminary survey results from 40 residents indicating high support for open space and affordable housing, though demographic data suggested a need for broader community outreach.

items.title: City Department and Board Testimony
items.summary: City officials discussed priorities including climate-resilient park features, the Walkling Court housing redevelopment, school playground accessibility, and a potential small grant program for private historic homes.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: A representative of Medford Youth Girls Softball requested CPA assistance for drainage, irrigation, and field maintenance at Tufts Park and Hickey Park.

items.title: Chevalier Theater Emergency Funding
items.summary: Approved an off-cycle application for $100,000 to restore the theater’s deteriorating facade and cornice after project bids significantly exceeded original estimates.

items.title: Administrative Items and Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes for the February 8 meeting and acknowledged the upcoming resignation of committee member Casey Hagerty.
